note: Twenty-five pages at 595.3x841.9 pt, 43 measured regions and 43 distinct page-plus-bbox keys. Twenty-five of them are the page-foot WeChat stamp standing alone at the identical [448.9,767.2,592.2,838.8] block of exactly 693 paths and 0.0205 area on every page, with no fused case anywhere - the cleanest furniture census in the block. The other eighteen hold sixteen exhibits: Figures 1 to 11 and Tables 1 to 5, both series complete, plus the second and third donut panels of Figure 2, which are excluded as duplicates so that one captioned figure is not counted three times. Every exhibit is cited by number, twenty-two numbered pointers in all, with three mentions a page ahead of their art (Table 2, Figures 6 and 7) and no exhibit cited twice. Figures and tables split by kind on caption side - all eleven captions below, all five tables above - and the gaps are tight and uniform (figures 14.6 to 15.7 pt; tables only 0.65 to 4.20 pt, with Table 1's caption line box overlapping its own grid by 1.6 pt, the block's first negative gap). Captions print 'Figure N:' / 'Table N:' with an ASCII colon sixteen times. Five figures print the same unit cube (Figures 3 to 7), so the drawing template is reused with only the contents changing, and the vector diagrams (3, 4, 5) are separated from the surfaced ones (6, 7) only by what is drawn inside. Raster resolution runs 171 dpi (Figure 1) to 424 dpi (Figure 7) with no distortion. Table 1 is booktabs with a doubled top and bottom rule and no vertical rule, Tables 2 to 5 are boxed, and Table 2 encodes its three merged dimension groups with four shades of grey fill rather than with borders. The page watermark prints as live text at y 307.5 and falls inside four exhibit boxes, including Figure 1's.
rules: Every exhibit is captioned and numbered - Figures 1 to 11 and Tables 1 to 5, both runs complete with no gap - and every one of the sixteen is cited by number, so this is the first paper in the block with a full citation set: sixteen rows, twenty-two numbered pointers, no uncited exhibit. [mention.count] is non-zero on every row.

Caption punctuation is one form only: 'Figure N:' and 'Table N:' with an ASCII colon on all sixteen. [caption.numbering] reads 'Figure N:' or 'Table N:' sixteen times; no full stop, no bare number, no all-capitals variant exists here.

Caption side splits by kind with no exception - all eleven figures print BELOW, all five tables ABOVE - and the gaps are tight and uniform: figures clear their box by 14.6 pt (Figure 2) to 15.7 pt, nine of the eleven inside 15.6-15.7, while tables sit only 0.65 to 4.20 pt above the grid. One table caption overlaps its own table: Table 1's caption line box runs 1.63 pt INTO the region top, so its gap is negative and a detector that requires the caption to clear the box misses it entirely. [caption.position] is 'below' on the eleven items and 'above' on the five tables, so kind, not paper style, decides the side in this document.

Mentions run ahead of the art more often than behind it: Table 2 is cited on p6 and prints on p7, Figure 6 is cited on p14 and prints on p15, Figure 7 is cited on p16 and prints on p17, so [mention.lead_pages] is 1 on three rows and 0 on the other thirteen. No exhibit is ever cited twice before it prints.

The paper repeats one drawing template four times: Figures 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 all print the same unit cube with ticks to 1.2 on all three axes, differing only in what is drawn inside it (vectors, vectors with legend, a shaded cap, a fan of trajectories). [geometry.three_d] is therefore non-'no' on eight of the eleven figures, and a family rule that keys on 'three axes' would call all eight the same family. They split by content instead: Figure 3 is flowchart-or-schematic (an annotated geometric diagram of the model), Figures 4, 5, 10 and 11 are surface-or-3D vector bundles and Figures 6 and 7 surface-or-3D meshes.

Two exhibits share one caption baseline: Figure 4 and Figure 5 print 'Figure 4: Application 1-4' at y 536.1 and 'Figure 5: Application 5-8' at y 537.4, 1.3 pt apart, and Tables 4 and 5 both at y 645.1 exactly. A caption-to-region join that works on y alone assigns both to one panel; [caption.verbatim] is the only disambiguator, and the x-ranges must be used.

The one caption-like line that is NOT a caption is p12's 'Figure 5.' at y 334.3 - the tail of the sentence 'We apply 3DVA to some countries and obtain the results shown as Figure 4 and Figure 5.' wrapped onto its own line, 200 pt above the art. A caption detector keyed on 'Figure N.' takes it as the figure's caption and leaves Figure 5 uncaptioned; [mention.lead_sentence] for Figure 5 is that same body line plus its wrapped tail.

Furniture leaks inside exhibit boxes: the page watermark prints as live TEXT at y 307.5 on every page, and that baseline falls inside SIX of the sixteen measured boxes - Figure 1 on p4, Table 1 on p5, Table 2 on p7, Figure 8 on p19 and BOTH panels of Figure 10/11 on p23 - so the row text of those exhibits begins with a WeChat id rather than with the caption. [place.area_frac] for those rows is set by the art, not by the watermark, and nothing in the record marks the intrusion.

Table grids are drawn as vector STROKES here, not as the sub-point fills of the previous two papers: Table 1 has 5 horizontal rules and zero verticals (booktabs, with doubled top and bottom rules at 302.0/304.9 and 606.4/609.3), Tables 2 to 5 are all boxed with both edges ruled. [table.rule_style] is therefore read off the stroke geometry, because a fill-based classifier reads 'no rules' off four tables that print closed grids and one booktabs table whose only fills are none.

Row counting from text baselines fails on two of the five tables: Table 1's descriptions wrap, giving 31 baselines for 17 rows, and Table 3 is transposed so its header row is eight country names and its stub column carries the metric names. [table.rows] the recorded row counts come from the rule geometry (17 = 5 rules over a 307.3 pt block at 18 pt per row; 3 = 4 rules; 5 = 6 rules; 13 from the fill bands).

Figure 2 is three DONUT charts, one per dimension, and each panel carries its own legend at its right edge - measured as a single row with panel_count 3 and legend 'outside-right'. [geometry.panel_count] is 3 on that row and 1 on every other, so this is the only multi-panel exhibit in the paper.

The paper's own vocabulary disagrees with its numbering twice: the caption of Figure 4 says 'Application 1-4' while the legend lists Standard plus USA, Japan, India and UK (four countries, so 1-4 counts only the countries), and Figure 5 says 'Application 5-8' for China, Australia, South Africa and Malaysia. Table 3's 'Deviation Angle' row carries its unit '(◦)' inside the stub cell rather than the header, so [table.units_in_header] is false on all five grids.

Two figures print no legend at all and say so nowhere: Figure 6's colour ramp and Figure 7's four trajectory colours are both unexplained, and Figure 9's legend keys intervention timing while its three trace colours (the SD/ST/SI dimensions) are named only in the running text. [geometry.colorbar] is false on all eleven figures - no figure in this paper has a colour key.

Resolution is uniformly high for a pasted-raster paper - 171 to 424 dpi, no 72 dpi survivors and no aspect distortion on any of the ten rasters - so [place.area_frac] and legibility are not inversely related here as they were in the previous paper.
